ontogeny.title: Ontogeny of simulation state fields for zebrafish (Danio rerio) and flying fish (Exocoetidae), per developmental stage
ontogeny.builder: session scratch builder (not in repo); SL, mass and fin ratios are read live from anatomy-model/parametric/stages.json so they match the anatomy model exactly
ontogeny.consumer: sim-engine/lib/state.mjs resolveState(organismDoc, ageDays). Interpolation rule: ONTOGENY.md, section "Interpolation rule".

conflicts.zf_mass_larval: Live larval masses (Bagatto 2001 Table 1: 0.33 mg at 3.9-4.0 mm, 1.38 mg at 6.4 mm, 3.69 mg at 8.2 mm) are 25-50% BELOW the Beaudouin 2015 law used for mass_kg (0.44, 2.1, 4.6 mg at those lengths, if Bagatto length is SL). Bouin-fixed masses (Rombough & Drader 2009: 0.16 mg at 7 dpf; 3.5 mg at 14.1 mm TL) are lower still, about 4-5x below the law at an assumed ~12 mm SL. Larval mass_kg is an upper bound.
conflicts.zf_growth_rate: Size at age depends on rearing: Bagatto 2001 larvae were 6.4 mm at ~26 dpf, while the repo curve (Parichy 0.32 mm/d) gives 11.0 mm at 26 dpf and Parichy group-reared rates (0.45-0.55 mm/d) reach 11 mm at 16-19 dpf. Age alone does not fix the state; SL does.
conflicts.zf_adult_mass: Adults of 34-36 mm SL weighed 0.84-0.90 g (Plaut & Gordon 1994; Plaut 2000), while the extrapolated Beaudouin law gives 0.54 g at 36 mm SL.
conflicts.zf_ucrit: Adult Ucrit 0.560 m/s wild-type and 0.437 m/s long-fin (Plaut 2000, 5-min steps) vs 0.238 m/s long-fin at the same 28 C (Wakamatsu 2019, 1-min steps, 170 ml tunnel): a ~2x protocol effect. Treat adult Ucrit as [0.24, 0.56] m/s.
conflicts.zf_metabolic_scaling: The larval law (46.1 M^0.825, 28 C) extrapolated to 0.84 g gives ~14 umol g-1 h-1, below Plaut & Gordon 1994 adult SMR 26.8-68.7 umol g-1 h-1 (28 C) but near Lucas & Priede 1992 (17.4 umol g-1 h-1 at 24 C, as quoted by Plaut & Gordon). No data bridge 3.5 mg to 0.27 g.
conflicts.ff_species_mix: Flying-fish rows mix H. affinis growth, Daane 2021 fin lengths (H. rondeleti, E. volitans, C. furcatus), Davenport 1992 exponents (E. obtusirostris) and the Park & Choi adult (C. hiraii, 0.06 kg at 0.203 m SL vs 0.13 kg for H. affinis at 0.206 m): mass at a given SL differs ~2x between sources.
